feature: A recording remembers where the pointer went and every click
summary: Every screen recording made in Photonz now keeps the pointer's path and each click (when, where, which button) in a small file beside the video, and opening the recording loads them. A recording without them can be given clicks by hand. Nothing draws them yet: ringing a click is the next task.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Record a region of the screen for about five seconds and click a few times inside it, then press Stop.
In the Screenshots folder, look beside the new MP4 for a file of the same name ending in .photonzpointer.
Open any recording, switch to Edit, put the playhead at two seconds, and right-click its clip on the timeline.
Choose Add Click at Playhead…, then click the picture where the click should be.
Press Command Z to take the click back; choose the row again and press Escape to call it off.
With a recording's clip selected, open the Clip menu: Add Click at Playhead… is there too.

evaluate: Did recording, and pressing Stop, feel exactly as quick as before?
After choosing Add Click at Playhead…, was it obvious the next click on the picture places it?
Is the Click added pill enough to know it worked, while nothing draws the click yet?
Is the clip's right-click menu the place you would look for this?
rough: Nothing on screen shows a recorded or added click yet: the ticks on the clip bar and the click ring are the next task (clicks in a recording can show an effect).
After Add Click at Playhead… the only sign the canvas is waiting is the crosshair over the picture; there is no hint line.

The walk cannot click on your screen, so its three clicks go in through the same door the Mac's mouse monitor feeds; a real click by a person has not been exercised by a walk. Their timing and placement match within a frame and two pixels, and the file's own length agrees with the clock the clicks are timed on.
A recording saved in the old recording window (which rewrites the file with the trim baked in) does not load its clicks, rather than loading them on the wrong frames.
Recording only covers a whole display or a region today; there is no window recording, so there is no window mapping to check.
No mock draws recorded clicks or a pointer path, so there is no frame to compare against.
